proseChanges.now: The Worker dispatches application HTTP to stateless ConversationSocket instances and forwards upgrades directly on hosts other than configured help hosts. Scratch first-request and warm maximum Worker CPU fell from 124/80 ms to 4/9 ms. The update uses the existing Durable Object class and binding and adds no migration.
proseChanges.ownerAction: Update from v0.4.52 without resetting. Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state, private settings and installation encryption custody. Stop the old Worker before updating and retain native owners, memberships, permissions, support history, files, erasure fences and all applied migration identities. Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and rer 0.2.142. The existing Wrangler migration `v1` already provisions `ConversationSocket` on v0.4.52. Keep that migration and the `CONVERSATIONS` binding in the deployment. The update adds no Wrangler or D1 migrations. For older installations, follow the upgrade steps in the intervening published releases and apply each missing migration once in filename order before serving HTTP or queue traffic. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before deploying. On the first hosted deploy, supply `--owner-name` if the installation has no saved owner name. Retain the durable recovery revocation watermark on rollback. Portable restore requires fresh Managed recovery and custody binding. To roll back this update, redeploy v0.4.52 (the restore point for the measured installation is Worker version `9b6ba461`).

publicReleaseNotes:
The Worker dispatches application HTTP to a pool of stateless `http:<shard>` instances of the existing `ConversationSocket` Durable Object. The pool stores no data. The Worker handles static assets and canonical redirects and forwards WebSocket upgrades directly to the conversation or project object. On a configured help host, the application checks the host policy before forwarding an upgrade. Socket handlers and scheduled discovery load on demand.

On the live v0.4.52 installation, ticket status updates, widget settings, Webhooks and the sitemap used 31–39 ms of Worker CPU. In scratch measurements the first-request and warm maxima fell from 124 and 80 ms to 4 and 9 ms, within the Workers Free 10 ms allowance. At ChargeDesk traffic levels, the estimated Durable Object volume is about 10,000 requests per day against the 100,000 daily allowance.

The update uses the existing Durable Object class and binding and adds no Wrangler or D1 migration.

Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and rer 0.2.142. The existing Wrangler migration `v1` already provisions `ConversationSocket` on v0.4.52. Keep that migration and the `CONVERSATIONS` binding in the deployment. The update adds no Wrangler or D1 migrations. For older installations, follow the upgrade steps in the intervening published releases and apply each missing migration once in filename order before serving HTTP or queue traffic. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before deploying. On the first hosted deploy, supply `--owner-name` if the installation has no saved owner name. Retain the durable recovery revocation watermark on rollback. Portable restore requires fresh Managed recovery and custody binding. To roll back this update, redeploy v0.4.52 (the restore point for the measured installation is Worker version `9b6ba461`).
